title: Add GitHub issue labels with AI using your rules
h1: ask ai to add the right labels to a github issue
description: Add the labels your team agrees on to a GitHub issue with AI. Existing labels stay, and a missing name becomes a new label, so spelling matters.
keyword: add github issue labels with ai
keywords: ai add labels to github issue
answer: **give every keyboard bug the same label, without losing the labels already there.** paste a github issue and the exact names to add. the bot keeps existing labels. missing names become new labels, so a typo becomes part of your system. label changes bypass sending approval; put an ask-first instruction in the job if you want a preview.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: consistent labels start with exact names.
what:
**make the next issue easier to find.** paste its link, or describe it so the bot can find it. give your allowed labels and what each means.

use the owner, repository and issue number together. "acessibility" becomes a real label if it does not exist. the bot adds labels without removing the ones already there.
uses: **missing steps:** add needs-reproduction after checking the report lacks them.
**keyboard trouble:** use your existing accessibility label for a navigation bug.
**wrong component:** add the agreed label for the affected part of the product.
**another look:** add a review label when the owner requests one.

routine.message: when a github issue opens in ticket-desk/box-office, read the report. propose access-check only for keyboard access problems. otherwise propose no label. show the issue number and the words supporting your choice here. ask me before you change anything. after i agree, add only access-check and report the saved labels. never create other spellings, remove labels or touch another repository.
routine.when: when an issue opens in ticket-desk/box-office
routine.needs: github read and write for this bot; allow issue reads and label addition in this repository
routine.output:
ticket-desk/box-office #28
- reporter: hannah
- evidence: the date picker cannot be reached with the keyboard.
- proposed label: access-check

proposed addition: access-check. current labels will stay.

steps: **name your labels.** connect github and give the bot the allowed spellings and meanings.
**keep its reach small.** allow read and write, limited to issue reads and label addition.
**try one report.** ask for the issue and proposed label before it changes anything.
**open the issue.** confirm the saved labels match your choice, then set the routine. pause it when label rules change.
watch: **your allowed list is the spelling guide.** missing names become labels. keep the routine to the names you gave it.
**use the full issue reference.** the same number can belong to a different repository.
**keep triage running overnight.** github events arrive at once. dusk cloud keeps the bot working while your computer sleeps.

faq.q: will this replace the labels already on the issue?
faq.a: **it adds to them.** existing labels stay. tell it to add only the one you named.

faq.q: what happens if the label does not exist?
faq.a: **github creates it.** exact spellings prevent a collection of bug, bugs and bug-report labels.

steps: ask for a proposal before any change
open the issue and read its labels

mistakes.fix: give it a short allowed list, with meanings.

mistakes.mistake: recognising the title and skipping the repository
mistakes.fix: match the owner, repository and issue number.

tip.text: agree on label names before you automate them.

worked.before: hannah reports a keyboard problem on issue #28. it currently has only bug.
worked.after: after your yes: bug and access-check. no extra spelling, no labels removed.
